extracted.intended_audience: Extramural NIH applicants (PD/PIs), institutional officials (AORs), and NIH program staff
extracted.subtask_short: NIH appeal of initial peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and acceptance criteria for submitting and processing appeals of the NIH initial peer review of competing grant applications, including allowable grounds, timing, submission/acknowledgement rules, and possible outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of an Appeal (four criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal is a written communication from a PD/PI and/or applicant institution that meets four criteria: (1) is received after issuance of the summary statement and up to 30 calendar days after the second level of peer review, (2) describes a flaw or perceived flaw in the review process for a particular application, (3) is based on one or more of four allowable issues, and (4) displays concurrence from the Authorized Organization Representative (AOR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All four conditions must be met for the submission to be treated as an appeal rather than a grievance; timing and AOR concurrence are mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance vs. Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: A grievance is a written communication from a PD/PI and/or applicant organization that presents concerns about the peer review process but does not meet the criteria for an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters that do not meet the appeal criteria and/or lack AOR concurrence will be handled as grievances according to IC-specific procedures rather than as appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and scope of the policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The revised policy applies to appeal letters with respect to the initial peer review of all competing applications submitted to the NIH for the January 25, 2011 due date and thereafter, including reviews conducted by CSR and by Institutes/Centers and applications (e.g., fellowships) that typically do not require Council review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy does not apply to appeals of technical evaluation of Research and Development contract projects, appeals of NIH funding decisions, or appeals of decisions concerning extensions of MERIT awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required preliminary step: consult the NIH Program Official (PO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting an appeal, the applicant should consider the summary statement and contact the appropriate NIH Program Official (PO) to discuss the summary statement and review outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PO can answer questions, advise on whether to modify or resubmit under NIH resubmission policies, or recommend submitting a substantially different new application. Contacting the PO is encouraged as an initial step; however, it does not replace filing an appeal if criteria are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on contacting SRG or Council members
rubrics_metrics.description: At no time should the PD/PI or an official of the applicant organization attempt to contact individual members of the Scientific Review Group (SRG) or members of the Council about the review of an application or appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contacting individual reviewers or Council members could jeopardize the confidentiality of the review process and is explicitly disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method and AOR concurrence requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal letter must be submitted (hard copy or electronically) to the PO and must display concurrence from the Authorized Organization Representative (AOR). The AOR must send the letter directly to the PO or send concurrence to the PD/PI who will forward materials and AOR concurrence to the PO. A communication from the PD/PI or institutional official only, or with a cc to the AOR, will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although content may originate from PD/PI or institutional officials, the AOR's direct transmission or stated concurrence is required. The PO will send an acknowledgement letter within 10 days of receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing constraints and IC deadline rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal must be received after the summary statement is issued and no later than 30 calendar days after the relevant Council meeting; ICs may establish earlier deadlines to have appeal letters available at Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In no circumstance will an appeal be accepted before the summary statement has been transmitted. IC-specific deadlines may apply for inclusion in Council materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal letter content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal letter will be accepted only if it (1) describes the flaws in the review process for the application in question, (2) explains the reasons for the appeal, and (3) is based on one or more allowable process-related issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters failing to describe flaws, explain reasons, or lacking allowable grounds will be considered grievances rather than appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed ground: Evidence of reviewer bias
rubrics_metrics.description: One allowable issue on which an appeal may be based is evidence of bias on the part of one or more peer reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letter must describe the bias and how it affected the review process; mere disagreement with reviewers does not constitute evidence of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed ground: Conflict of interest (COI) per 42 CFR 52h.5
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals may be based on a conflict of interest as specified in regulation at 42 CFR 52h.5 (Scientific Peer Review of Research Grant Applications and Research and Development Contract Projects) on the part of one or more peer reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals involving potential COI or violations of ethical conduct rules on the part of NIH staff or other federal employees will be referred to the appropriate Deputy Ethics Counselor before further review or action on the appeal is taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed ground: Lack of appropriate expertise within the SRG
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal may be based on a lack of appropriate expertise within the Scientific Review Group that reviewed the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letter should explain how the absence of necessary expertise affected the review and the evaluation of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed ground: Factual errors by reviewers that could have altered outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal may be based on factual error(s) made by one or more reviewers that could have substantially altered the outcome of the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appellant must identify specific factual errors and explain why correction of those errors could reasonably have changed the review result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific-opinion-only appeals are not acceptable
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal letters based solely on differences of scientific opinion will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disagreement with reviewers' scientific judgments, absent procedural flaws or factual errors, should be addressed via resubmission or revised application rather than appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH staff evaluation and possible re-review
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH review staff and program staff will consider the basis of the appeal and evaluate its merit; if both review staff and program staff support an appeal, the original application, without additional materials or modifications, will be re-reviewed by the same or a different SRG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the results of the re-review (not the first review) are made available to Council, and information about the appeal is not made available to Council in that case.

rubrics_metrics.name: When staff do not support the appeal: withdrawal or Council availability
rubrics_metrics.description: If review staff and program staff do not support the appeal (or do not agree on its merit), the PD/PI and/or institutional official may elect to withdraw the appeal; if not withdrawn, the appeal letter will be made available to Council. The IC may not deny the PD/PI or applicant organization the opportunity to have an appeal letter made available to Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A withdrawal request must be submitted to the PO and display concurrence from the AOR; procedural rules for how the AOR must transmit concurrence mirror the submission rules for appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council consideration outcomes and finality
rubrics_metrics.description: Only two outcomes are possible after Council consideration: (1) Council may concur with the appeal and recommend that the application be re-reviewed, or (2) Council may concur with the SRG's recommendation and deny the appeal. No action by Council is equivalent to denial. The Council's recommendation is final and will not be considered again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellants should be aware that even evident factual errors may be deemed unlikely to have altered the outcome, and thus Council can deny appeals on that basis; contacting Council members is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-review conditions and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If Council recommends re-review, the original application will be re-reviewed without additional materials or modifications, possibly by the same or a different SRG; re-review will typically mean reassignment to a subsequent review round and delay in the final funding decision. The outcome of the re-review is final and cannot be appealed again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit additional materials or attempt to amend the application during the appeal/re-review process; the re-review uses only the original submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution communication timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Secretary for the Council will communicate the Council recommendation to the PD/PI, AOR, and NIH staff with a need to know. If the appeal was received by the IC deadline, a written explanation of the resolution will be provided no later than 30 calendar days after the Council meeting; if received after the IC deadline, the Executive Secretary will provide, no more than 30 calendar days after receipt, a written explanation of the IC's plan for making the appeal available to Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These timelines govern when applicants should expect written communication about the resolution or the plan to make the appeal available to Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral of staff-related ethical/COI issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals that involve potential conflict of interest or violation of ethical conduct rules on the part of NIH staff or other federal employees will be referred to the appropriate Deputy Ethics Counselor for consideration and resolution before any further review or action is taken on the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such referrals may delay consideration of the appeal while ethics reviews are completed.
